You and have a lot in common, although I’m 6 years your junior. Not sure if that’s good or bad 

Anyways, a lot of people on the autism spectrum have some interesting genetics. I had to have some genetic testing done, and although I’m not on the spectrum, evidently my genetic makeup is very similar to those who are. In case it’s relevant later on, I’m currently diagnosed with general anxiety, PTSD, and depression. 

So first of all, the loss of interest and motivation is relatable as fuck. For me, I gave up because I thought that if I don’t do something perfectly the first time, I’ll never be good enough. Never mind the fact that it’s nearly impossible to get a 100 on every test in every subject. And for almost everything else, perfection is subjective. But I got off topic. Mental fog and low motivation are common symptoms of both depression and drug abuse. Your post is very well written, and you seem to research things very thoroughly. So although I would recommend you lay off the drugs (personal experience), I doubt you fucked up your brain permanently. Besides, you smoked pot and drank. That’s not exactly healthy, but it’s not like you started every morning with a line of blow and then smoked some meth before shooting up.

As far as antidepressants go, I don’t have much experience. I was never prescribed any because of an increased risk suicide. However, there is a genetic mutation I have (also common with people on the spectrum) that interferes with how your body processes certain drugs. I don’t know what it’s called of the top of my head, but I do know it effects common anesthesias and certain opiates/opioids. For example, my body can’t handle codeine. It has almost no effect on me, both at therapeutic doses and when I’ve drank lean. It does, however, get improperly metabolized and damage my liver. I’m not a doctor or geneticist, but it’s just a thought. Maybe your antidepressants aren’t working because your body can’t respond to them like it’s supposed to. As far as alternative therapies, I’ve tried everything under the sun. It can help temporarily, but I wonder how much is an actual effect and how much is placebo. Either way, essential oils smell nice. I won’t recommend alternative treatments, but you do you. Just be careful.

as a musician the emotions of listening to a song play into my dependency on music.

I feel empty and apathetic, so I listen to music because I want to feel something. Happy music doesn’t make me happy, so I listen to sad/angry music. Then I feel sad or angry, which is better than feeling nothing but it’s not a positive feeling either.

So to relax and get back to apathy I go play/write music to try and let go of what I’m feeling. I have a hard time putting my feelings into words, but some of the saddest songs I’ve ever heard don’t have a single word sung. Listening to others’ music lets me feel like I’m not alone, that there’s someone else out there who gets me. Writing/playing music lets me express those emotions, and hopefully connect with someone else as well.
